title: Oscillating prefetch orchestrator for mixed-length continuous scheduler tuning
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (web chat + API summarization) cause the continuous-batcher to oscillate between aggressive prefetching and conservative slot allocation. That oscillation increases GPU memory churn and KV cache fragmentation, resulting in 10-25% tail latency spikes and up to 12% higher memory pressure on p4d nodes in production.

Goal: Reduce oscillation and stabilize KV residency while preserving user-facing latency SLOs for short-turn interactive flows and long-turn generation. Implement a scheduler-level damping mechanism ("oscillation damping") and a KV bank rebalancer that proactively coils prefetched KV into compact banks to reduce fragmentation during bursts. Validate on stage with synthetic mixed-length traces and a small customer synthetic traffic test.

Context: We've tuned length-aware batching and prefetch windows independently, but the coupling between slot admission, prefetch aggressiveness, and KV compaction hasn't been addressed holistically. Recent postmortems (ENG-472888) show repeated GC-like KV evictions during microbursts of long responses interleaved with many short prompts. This ticket explores a runtime-level orchestrator to smooth prefetch decisions across time windows and GPU memory banks.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce an Oscillation Damping Controller (ODC) in the continuous scheduler that maintains a short-term history (decay window) of prefetch aggression metrics (avg_prefetch_tokens, prefetch_rate_variance). ODC maps variance to a damping factor that scales prefetch window and slot tenure. 2) Implement KV Bank Rebalancer: group KV residency by contiguous allocation banks and apply a lightweight compaction pass during low-utilization windows (inter-burst). 3) Add a GPU slab watermark to prevent prefetch if slab fragmentation exceeds threshold. 4) Expose new config flags (odc.enabled, odc.decay_ms, kv.rebalance_threshold, gpu.slab_watermark_pct) and safety caps for dedicated environments. 5) Run A/B stage rollout with canary traffic and continuous tracing to measure tail latency, memory churn, and eviction frequency.
acceptance_criteria: Stage experiments show >=15% reduction in 95th token latency for mixed-length synthetic traces compared to baseline
KV eviction events per minute reduced by >=30% on p4d-stage during representative microburst tests
GPU memory fragmentation metric (slab_unused_fragment) drops by >=10 percentage points during steady state
No regression (>5%) in median latency for short-turn interactive flows
Config flags and metrics emitted to console: odc.damping_factor, kv.bank_count, gpu.slab_watermark
experiment_plan: Create synthetic workload generator with configurable mix ratio of short (<=8 tokens) and long (>=1024 tokens) turns
Run baseline 24h run capturing slot allocation traces, prefetch metrics, kv eviction logs, slab fragmentation histograms
Implement ODC prototype behind runtime feature flag and run 24h A/B with 10% traffic canary
Add KV Bank Rebalancer in a subsequent run, measure incremental impact
Collect traces: per-request kv_residency_time, prefetch_tokens, eviction_reason, slab_fragmentation_percent
Iterate damping parameters with grid search: decay_ms in {50,100,200,500}, damping_scale in {0.5,0.75,0.9}
Document config defaults and safe fallbacks for Dedicated customers (allow disabling rebalancer)
results_summary: Initial stage runs (odc prototype only) reduced prefetch rate variance by ~40% and decreased 95th token latency by 9% for a 70/30 short/long mix. However, KV eviction rate only fell 12% indicating compaction is necessary. The KV Bank Rebalancer prototype (background compaction during low-util windows) cut eviction rate by 36% and reduced slab_unused_fragment from 28% to 17% in burst-heavy traces. Median latency for short-turns increased ~3% in one parameter set (decay_ms=50, damping_scale=0.5) — we reverted to decay_ms=200, damping_scale=0.75 which preserved median latency and kept 95th improvements. GPU overhead of rebalancer background compaction is ~1.7% additional kernel time during low-util windows. Overall results meet acceptance targets after parameter tuning.
blockers: Need kernel-level allocator metric exposure (ENG-314159) to compute slab_unused_fragment accurately
Dependence on Dedicated QA cluster free capacity for 48h A/B (scheduling conflict)
